worked: Married filing combined (joint federal), ages 60 and 62. Each spouse has a 6,000 of their own: person 0's 10,000 is limited to 6,000, and the 3,000 of room person 1 leaves unused does not pass to person 0. Taxable income is 0 here, so the amount shows only in relief_amounts: a joint return under the 32,000 limit falls under the 31,500 standard deduction once the exemption is taken. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages 18,000.00 + IRA distributions 13,000.00 = 31,000.00. Federal taxable income = 31,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 0.00 (floored at 0) (federal senior deduction ignored). Form MO-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 31,000.00. Line 2 additions 0.00. Line 3 total income 31,000.00. Line 4 subtractions 0.00. Line 6 Missouri adjusted gross income 31,000.00 - 0.00 = 31,000.00. Section B: Line 1 31,000.00; Line 2 0.00; Line 3 31,000.00; Line 4 32,000.00; Line 5 0.00; Line 6Y 10,000.00, Line 7Y 6,000.00; Line 6S 3,000.00, Line 7S 3,000.00; Line 8 9,000.00; Line 9 9,000.00. Projection, each person: person 0 6,000.00 - 0.00 = 6,000.00; person 1 3,000.00 - 0.00 = 3,000.00; total 9,000.00. Form MO-1040 Line 8 pension and Social Security exemption 9,000.00. Lines 9-13 federal income tax deduction not applied (not modelled; the household's federal tax is not an input). Line 14 standard deduction 31,500.00. Line 26 subtotal 31,000.00 - 9,000.00 - 31,500.00 = -9,500.00 (below 0, so 0.00: taxable income is floored at 0). Line 29 taxable income 0.00. Tax 0.00 (nothing taxable). state_agi (after every relief, as the check format defines it) = Line 6 31,000.00 - Line 8 9,000.00 = 22,000.00; the form's Missouri AGI is Line 6, 31,000.00.
accepted_approximations: The federal income tax deduction is not applied (not_modelled).
